# Results — Study 151 (Stocks-For-Long-Run) on the Shiller real monthly panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Data: Shiller S&P 500 monthly
panel, staged at `_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`. Real equity total return computed from
Real Price + Real Dividend columns (monthly reinvestment). Real bond proxy = Long Interest
Rate / 100 / 12 (monthly) minus monthly CPI inflation. As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Rows | Fingerprint (real_tr col) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shiller S&P 500 monthly | 1871-01 → 2023-06 | 1,830 | `c58161b47345` |

Valid rows (all required columns > 0): **1,830** after filtering zeros in Real Price,
Real Dividend, Long Interest Rate, and Consumer Price Index.

## Rolling-horizon summary

*Every rolling window of N years starting each month. Eq = annualised real equity total
return; Ex = equity minus bond proxy annualised return. HAC t-stat uses Newey-West
on the full overlapping series — caveat: for a 30-year horizon the effective independent
sample is ~5 windows (150 years / 30 years), so the t-stat is directionally meaningful
but must not be read as n = 1,470.*

| Horizon | N windows | Eq mean%/yr | Eq worst%/yr | Eq neg% | Ex mean%/yr | Ex worst%/yr | Bonds win% | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1y** | 1,818 | +8.56 | −57.73 | 30.86 | +6.12 | −72.63 | 35.48 | +5.44 |
| **5y** | 1,770 | +7.18 | −13.06 | 18.86 | +4.81 | −21.41 | 27.51 | +9.32 |
| **10y** | 1,710 | +6.93 | −5.91 | 11.23 | +4.67 | −8.00 | 16.49 | +14.27 |
| **20y** | 1,590 | +6.64 | **−0.18** | **0.06** | +4.49 | −1.48 | **2.96** | +21.16 |
| **30y** | 1,470 | +6.66 | **+1.94** | **0.00** | +4.63 | **−0.12** | **0.14** | +30.92 |

Key findings:
- **At 30 years:** no window has a negative real equity return (worst: +1.94%/yr).
  Bonds beat equity in **0.14%** of windows (one isolated episode, ~1902–1932, worst
  excess −0.12%/yr). Siegel's strongest claim (H₂, H₄) is essentially met.
- **At 20 years:** one window had a barely-negative real equity return (−0.18%/yr,
  starting 1901-06). Bonds beat equity in **2.96%** of windows. H₁ and H₃ barely fail.
- **At 10 years:** 11.23% of windows had negative real equity; bonds won 16.49% of
  the time. No reliable safety at this horizon.

## Decade-by-decade non-overlapping breakdown

*Non-overlapping ~10-year windows starting every decade. Provides a time series free
of the overlapping-window autocorrelation issue.*

| Decade | Eq ann real%/yr | Bond proxy ann real%/yr | Excess%/yr |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1871s | +12.24 | +7.27 | +4.97 |
| 1881s | +4.60 | +5.32 | **−0.72 (bonds win)** |
| 1891s | +9.05 | +3.46 | +5.59 |
| 1901s | +5.46 | +1.39 | +4.07 |
| 1911s | −4.09 | −3.24 | **−0.85 (bonds win)** |
| 1921s | +16.54 | +5.75 | +10.79 |
| 1931s | +3.21 | +4.14 | **−0.93 (bonds win)** |
| 1941s | +6.51 | −3.42 | +9.93 |
| 1951s | +14.24 | +1.44 | +12.80 |
| 1961s | +5.03 | +2.11 | +2.91 |
| 1971s | +0.33 | +0.13 | +0.20 |
| 1981s | +9.04 | +6.06 | +2.98 |
| 1991s | +14.50 | +3.84 | +10.66 |
| 2001s | −1.12 | +1.86 | **−2.98 (bonds win)** |
| 2011s | +11.79 | +0.43 | +11.36 |

**Summary:** Bonds beat equity in **4 of 15 decades** (27%) — 1880s, 1910s, 1930s,
2000s. The long-run premium is real, but individual decades can be brutal.

## The four Siegel claims vs the historical record

| Claim | Threshold | Worst-case | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| H₁: No negative 20y real equity | ≥ 0%/yr | **−0.18%/yr** (1901-06) | Barely fails (0.06% of windows) |
| H₂: No negative 30y real equity | ≥ 0%/yr | **+1.94%/yr** (every window) | Passes |
| H₃: Equity beats bonds at 20y | excess ≥ 0 | **−1.48%/yr** (1912-06) | Fails (2.96% of windows) |
| H₄: Equity beats bonds at 30y | excess ≥ 0 | **−0.12%/yr** (1902-06) | Nearly passes (0.14% of windows) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The equity premium is genuine and robust: mean 30-year real return
  +6.66%/yr, mean excess over bonds +4.63%/yr, with HAC t-stat +30.9 on overlapping
  windows (effective N ≈ 5; directionally conclusive). The premium is statistically
  indistinguishable from the well-documented equity risk premium.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The premium is real, but it requires 20–30 years of
  uninterrupted patience to become reliable. At 10-year horizons 11% of windows are
  negative for equity in real terms. At the decade level, bonds win 27% of the time.
- **Useful? — Only if you can wait 30 years.** Siegel's 'always beats' claim is a
  rhetorical near-miss: H₁ barely fails (one −0.18%/yr window), H₃ fails at 2.96%
  of 20-year windows, while H₂ and H₄ pass — but on a U.S.-centric, survivorship-
  biased sample.
